object: data: two rows in public.places share the slug 'sacramento'
why: A city and its county legitimately share a name, and the place tree allows it. bySlug() resolves the collision by ranking kinds — neighborhood, then city, then county — so a lookup is deterministic rather than arbitrary. That is a mitigation, not a fix: nobody has confirmed the two rows are the intended city and county rather than a seeding mistake.
cost_if_forgotten: A scoped link resolves to the wrong geography and nobody notices, because both answers look plausible. The heuristic makes it deterministic and therefore silent.
revisit_if: ANY of: a member reports results from the wrong area; a third row appears with the same slug; the Browse query rewrite (T156) starts reading places by slug; or 2026-11-30 passes.
